messages.author: 71171f0d61fc140f
messages.subject: stat_summary() on two dimensions
parts:
Hi All,

I'm wondering if stat_summary() can be used on two two dimensions
simultaneously. Specifically, I would like to plot the mean location
of a category in two dimensional space.

df <-data.frame(Categories = c(rep("A",100), rep("B", 100)),
Dim1 = c(rnorm(100,mean = -1), rnorm(100,1)),
Dim2 = c(rnorm(100,mean = -1), rnorm(100,1)) )

p <- ggplot(df, aes(Dim1, Dim2, colour = Categories))
p+geom_point()

Now, I'd figure if there were a way to do this with stat_summary(), it
would look like this

p + stat_summary(fun.x = testmean, fun.y = testmean, geom = "point")

But it actually plots all the points again. I figure it's producing
the mean value of each point. Is there a way to do this with
stat_summary(), or will I have to just do the summary outside of
ggplot?

-Joe

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: stat_summary() on two dimensions
parts:
Hi Joe,

You're best off just calculating the values yourself:

means <- ddply(df, "Categories", summarise, Dim1 = mean(Dim1), Dim2 =
mean(Dim2))

ggplot(df, aes(Dim1, Dim2, colour = Categories)) +
geom_point() +
geom_point(data = means, size = 5)

Hadley
